thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: sustained 5xx spike (10m window) on inference-gateway-ca-central-1 — error rate 18% (baseline 0.3%). Paging on-call.
Ryan (on-call): Got the page, looking now. @Samir can you pull the gateway and mlworker metrics for ca-central-1?
Samir: pulling dashboards. Gateway 502/504s spiking at 18% as noted. egress errors to model-backend show timeout errors (connect_timeout). mlworker pod restarts look normal. KV-cache miss rate up ~30%.
Maya: seeing latency increase on prefix-cache hits too, curious. Could be high tail due to a downstream TLS handshake issue to model-serving cluster.
Riley: any deploys in last hour to that region? I see no infra deploys, but a traffic policy update went out 9m ago to enable region-aware batching for a subset of customers.
Ryan (on-call): rollback traffic policy? Worth testing. Samir, can you run a quick curl against the model endpoint from the gateway box?
Samir: running now.
Samir: ```
curl -v "https://model-svc.ca-central.internal/v1/health" -H "Host: model-svc" --connect-timeout 2
* Connected to 10.12.5.22 (10.12.5.22) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* curl: (28) Operation timed out after 2001 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```
Samir: TLS handshake timing out from some gateway nodes to a subset of model-svc replicas.
Devon (runtime): That smells like a NAT/egress scaling problem — ephemeral ports exhausted or SYN backlog on the replicas. Can someone check conntrack / NAT exhaustion on the border nodes?
Riley: I can check NAT tables on the edge pool. Also noting the batcher change increased parallel connections per request slightly.
Lina (support): Customer-impact: Support routing shows 12 customers reporting errors from ca-central in the last 10m, mostly short requests that now return 502.
Kate (product): Which tier customers? Any enterprise customers impacted? Need to notify account teams if there's sustained degradation.
Ryan (on-call): Samir, gather a list of affected IPs and replica IDs. Riley, check conntrack counters. If NAT ports are the issue, we can shift some traffic to secondary egress pool.
Samir: affected replicas: model-svc-ca-c-1a [replica-id: r-7f2], r-7f3, r-8a1. IPs: 10.12.5.22, 10.12.5.23, 10.12.6.11. Logs show slow TLS accept: "accept tcp: i/o timeout" repeated.
Riley: conntrack table on edge-proxy-nyca-01: entries 999800 / max 1,000,000; ephemeral ports usage ~96%. Several edge nodes at 95%+. Egress pool 1 is saturated.
Devon (runtime): ok confirmed. Immediate mitigation: shift 30% of traffic for ca-central to egress-pool-2 (secondary NAT) and throttle batch parallelism to reduce new connections. I'll prepare commands.
Ryan (on-call): Do it. Also initiate routing fallback to us-east-2 for non-low-latency-critical customers.
Devon (runtime): patch ready. Commands:
```bash
# reduce batching parallelism
redwoodctl config set region=ca-central-1 batch.parallelism=1 --workspace=inference
# steer portion of egress
redwoodctl route adjust --region ca-central-1 --egress-pool egress-pool-2 --percent 30
```
Devon (runtime): executing now.
Samir: after steer, 5xx rate dropped to 11% in 2m.
Maya: KV-cache miss still high; might be downstream replica churn causing cold cache. We should enable prefix caching at the gateway for a short window to reduce some load.
Ryan (on-call): Agree. Riley, can you flip prefix cache TTL to 30s for ca-central? That should reduce backend hits.
Riley: on it.
Riley: ```
redwoodctl feature toggle prefix-cache --region ca-central-1 --ttl 30s
```
Lina (support): Logging comms: posting to status page draft: "We are experiencing elevated errors in ca-central-1 affecting inference requests. We have implemented traffic-steering mitigations and expect partial recovery; engineering is working on a full fix." Want approval before publishing.
Kate (product): publish with note about mitigation and ETA 30-60m, mention potential customer-specific reroutes. Tag accounts with active incidents.
Ryan (on-call): Approved. Lina, publish and escalate to account execs for enterprise customers.
Lina (support): Published and pinged account execs. Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RC-3241598765
Samir: collecting pcap from one gateway node to analyze TLS hangs.
Devon (runtime): observation: many TLS sessions in SYN_RECV on model-svc side, and kernel logs show "SYN cookies enabled" around the spike time. Likely transient backlog. Increasing accept queue and ephemeral port range on model-svc hosts will help long-term.
Maya: as medium-term fix, can we enable keepalive reuse / TLS session resumption on the gateway so subsequent requests don't initiate full handshake? That will reduce connections.
Devon (runtime): yes, we have a feature flag to enable session tickets on the gateway - I'll prepare a controlled rollout in ca-central.
Ryan (on-call): For now, monitor for 15 minutes. If 5xx < 5% and customer reports drop, we can close the page. If metrics rebound, escalate to infra pager.
Samir: 5xx at 4.6% now, latency back near baseline for most nodes. KV-cache miss down to 12%.
Riley: conntrack counts falling on edge nodes as expected after traffic-steer. Good.
Lina (support): customers still reporting a few errors but much reduced. Filing post-incident note and collecting affected request ids.
Kate (product): thanks all. Add action items: increase conntrack table on model-svc hosts, expand egress pool capacity for ca-central, enable TLS session resumption feature flag, and review recent batcher policy change that increased parallel connections.
Ryan (on-call): agreed. I'll open follow-up tickets and assign owners. Marking incident as mitigated; keeping thread open for postmortem notes.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Ryan (on-call). No further pages.
Ryan (on-call): closing the active paging loop. TY everyone. :thumbsup:
